text.p: Fibreboard Corp said Monday its more than $3 billion asbestos insurance settlement agreement is final.
In response to the final approval, Arthur Andersen LLP has removed its qualification regarding asbestos from its report on Fibreboard's 1995 financial statements, the company said.
Additionally, Fibreboard's insurers are commencing to pay about $1 billion in deferred settlement obligations.
The period for filing a petition for U.S. Supreme Court review of the settlement approved in July by the U.S. Fifth Circuit Court of appeals has expired, the company explained.

Fibreboard said the company's agreement with its insurers, CNA Financial Corp's Continental Casualty Co and Chubb Corp's Pacific Indemnity Co, is the nation's largest recorded single-company asbestos settlement.

A related global settlement agreement, which if ultimately approved supercedes the insurance settlement agreement, also was approved by the Fifth Circuit in July, but separately awaits that Court's decision on a pending petition for rehearing by objectors.
Under the agreement, Fibreboard said, its insurers will pay in full all settlements reached prior to August 27, 1993.

Additionally, the insurers will provide Fibreboard up to $2 billion, plus accrued interest, in additional funds to manage and resolve pending unsettled claims as of August 27, 1993, as well as claims filed after that date.
The settlement "is a major milestone in resolving our asbestos litigation and continuing Fibreboard's turn-around strategy," said chief executive John D. Roach.
"We now know for the first time that we are assured at a minimum of receiving the enormous benefits provided by the insurance settlement agreement.
"We can now focus all our attention on our next significant growth phase, with the goal of doubling revenues to $1 billion by the year 2000."
Revenues were $493 million last year, the company noted.

With the 1994 - 1995 acquisitions of Norandex and Vytec respectively, Fibreboard now is the fifth largest manufacturer of vinyl siding in North America, with a new manufacturing facility increasing plant capacity by more than 30 percent by mid-1997.
The company said it has set the objective of being in the "top three" by the turn of the century when analysts estimate that the vinyl siding market will reach some 4 billion square feet of product.
The company divested its Wood Products division in September 1995 and anticipates completing the sale of its Resorts Group by the end of this year.

The company said its growth goals focus on expanding market share in the building products industry through internal growth and acquisition with more than $200 million available through credit facilities to support expansion plans. -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.
